details: Stronger-than-expected US jobs data for August, showing 162,000 non-farm payrolls added and a steady 4.1% unemployment rate, has increased the probability of a Federal Reserve interest rate hike in September to around 60%. This data led to a retreat in Bitcoin's price below $80,000, as higher interest rates typically weigh on speculative assets like cryptocurrencies by increasing the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding investments. Investors are now closely watching upcoming inflation data (PPI on Thursday, CPI on Friday) for further clues on the Fed's policy path.
title: Strong US Jobs Data Pushes Bitcoin Below $80K as Fed Hike Bets Rise

details: The Liquid Network, a settlement platform often used by cryptocurrency exchanges, temporarily halted new transactions after approximately $320 million worth of Bitcoin was withdrawn from its federation wallet in a security exploit. This incident raises renewed concerns about the security infrastructure within the digital asset space.
title: Bitcoin-Linked Liquid Network Hit by $320 Million Security Exploit

details: Despite recent macroeconomic uncertainties and Bitcoin's price pullback, US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) recorded approximately $1 billion in net inflows last week, with a significant single-day inflow of $730.8 million on September 3rd. This sustained institutional demand provides a level of underlying support for the crypto market, even as short-term sentiment is influenced by Fed policy expectations.
title: US Spot Bitcoin ETFs See Net Inflows Despite Macro Headwinds

details: Brent crude prices climbed to around $97 a barrel on Monday due to escalating military tensions between the United States and Iran, which raised concerns over potential supply disruptions in the Middle East. Higher oil prices contribute to inflationary pressures, which could further influence the Federal Reserve's monetary policy decisions and, in turn, impact risk assets like cryptocurrencies.
title: Escalating US-Iran Tensions Push Oil Prices Higher, Adding to Market Pressure
